raw.cause: logger's channel was created with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY (flags 0x4b), so when logger receives nav's MsgSend it keeps its own priority 10 instead of inheriting nav's 30 (nav runs at 30 because it inherits display's priority). While nav is REPLY-blocked, media at priority 20 preempts logger. A 2 ms log reply takes up to ~49 ms; for example, message 109849 is received at 5432.8 ms but replied only at 5482.1 ms, while media runs on both CPUs.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (run_logger); nav's MsgSend to logger waits behind priority-20 media
raw.fix_summary: Drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so logger's receiving thread inherits the client's priority, as on any normal channel; or simply serve it via name_attach(). If logging really must not compete with real work, change the contract instead: make the log path asynchronous (MsgSendPulse or a local queue drained by a low-priority thread) so nav never REPLY-blocks on logger.

finding: nav waits on logger behind lower priority work
